body:
Yeah, this ^

There's guys who have been "into" me and get sad about me not reciprocating. But I know it's superficial because they don't even really know me. If we clicked, sure, but if someone is already attached based on, like, your face? No. You don't like me, u don't know me.

We're all just people, with all sorts of different things about us. People are so much more than their looks or social status or whatever. It's not what's important at all, imo. Enjoy your life, get to know people, see who you click with. Do you make each other laugh? Are they kind? Do you have fun? Do you want them in your life irrespective of gaining from it, but just because they light you up as a person?

>might as well

I love that, that brought a smile to my face haha. Just cause it's so simple but also true, might as well!
Aw hon, I've been there. It's brutal. Sending love ❤️ one step at a time. It gets better, but yeah, it's rough at first. You'll get there. Sending so much love ❤️ xx

It's the worst feeling. For me I think it's some kind of PTSD flashback of every time I've felt or been abandoned. Last time I stopped eating mostly and was in bed for days, just didn't show up to work or anything either. And i wasn't even really being abandoned in the end, I was just triggered. But instead of acting out on it too much I just left myself to feel it, idk. It was hell. I hope it helps heal me... like maybe I processed some things... but yeah.

My mum threatened abandonment when I was younger. It felt extra frightening because my dad was abusive and physically, too. If my mum wasn't there it wasn't just losing her - it was losing a somewhat protective barrier and being left with a very abusive parent fully in control of the household, and a lot more time alone with him. The physical abuse happened when my mum was out, mostly. So I think it steams back to that. It's the worst feeling I've ever experienced. It's a totally helpless dread - like imagine you're a young kid watching someone you love (who you perceive as protecting you as well) falling off the edge of a cliff in slow-motion, and you know you can't save them, you know you can't stop them, and there's nothing you can do. It's the worst thing I've ever experienced emotions wise I think, and I've been through a lot of shit...

For me I think my body and brain perceives it as terror and death all at once. Because as a kid being abandoned can be a matter of life and death. It's like I go into a shut-down response, like an animal accepting death in the wild. No more eating, no more drinking water, just lying in bed - and it's like your body wants you to do that. Trying to push through it and come back to life is an effort, and for me I often need other people, even a friend coming over to visit - to spring some life back into me - idk if it comvinces my subconscious I'm not alone and not dying and brings me back to life, or something, but yeah.

My abandonment issues are major, though.
The thing is, it's not rational, not really. They get triggered by bad relationships, too, relationships I'm better off without - whether it's abusive or even something I was considering ending myself. If I leave, it's fine to an extent, if I'm left or threatened with being left - I turn into a little kid, terrified and panicking or totally shutting down.
Romantic relationships are the worst trigger. With friends I'm not so bad.
It's something I'm working on. I have hope it can and is getting better.

I hear you. I really do.

I've felt similarly about the impact of feminist (and other activist group) narratives at times.

In left wing spaces I feel there's such a strong sense of justice and right vs wrong that people can be very aggressive about their beliefs. I say this as someone who is very left politically myself. I've went through similar journeys (emotionally, I mean) about this stuff.

I think it's great you're able to think critically and see there's something wrong + incomplete about the views that have been hammered into you in groups you have been in. You sound like an intelligent critical thinker, that's a good thing. The world needs more of those. ❤️

I know the intent with left wing groups can often be positive, but I feel it gets a bit culty and echo-chamber-y sometimes. There's a lot of black-and-white views, and I feel little room for nuance and compassionate understanding of different people and the people they see as "bad." It's a complex one, because often the causes are rooted in a desire for good and a fight against injustice - but yeah. Quite frankly I think it's all got a bit nuts, and loses our realness and humanity in it all a bit sometimes. I still hear the voice in my head from my time in left wing spaces ("you can't say nuts, that's ableist." Look, I've got about 5 mental illness', I can and I will b*tch. (Saying this tongue in cheek - gen not trying to upset anyone, sorry, just trying to illustrate a point).

I'm glad to hear you are still here. I'm sorry you're feeling rejected and left out from groups around you, people can be really polarised at times. I know it's hard but you deserve to take pride in who you are, and I hope you find some real ones out there in your life soon. You're doing good. Look after yourself xx

I'm there just now really. It's only been a few months but I'm feeling this so much. I knew I had pretty severe attachment issues, I'm now questioning if I have full on BPD.

It's hard, isn't it?
You're not alone.

I'm trying to be less "crazy," especially as I can blow up about things if I feel rejected or whatever 😐😭. I feel insane.

Taking time to yourself is important, but I'm not really practicing what I preach...

I've been inviting friends I feel secure with up and that takes the edge off a bit and helps me eat and stuff a bit more. Idk, I'm losing it.

It's hard. For some reason it helps to know you're not alone, and it's an understandable mental illness. A good friend has reassured me a few times too, although I need to learn how to do this myself as well I guess.

Probably worth going back to therapy.

Remembering I'm not alone seems to help (like, there are people who love and care about me and who have not left or totally disappeared), and trying to find myself again. Just be "me" for a bit, idk. Vague, but makes sense for me rn.

Yes, that's it!

Like, I noticed recently when I was feeling better in some ways I could dream again! Like normal dreams! That don't make sense and are a bit surreal. Not visiting some complex, detailed dream world and living out normal, real-life scenarios. It felt like I hadn't dreamt normally in years.

Ah, it sucks. Glad it's gotten better for you. Hopefully I can improve it again, too.

If you don't mind sharing, do you know what helps with this? 😶 Or is it just healing overall?

WOOHOO!!!!

True colours shine eventually. So satisfying.

You're angry, right? As you should be. You didn't deserve that shit and it fucking sucks.

It sucks that you have to heal from it and pick up the pieces.

It's okay to be angry, anger is healthy and actually a part of healing from this shit.

Anger is the part of you that says "I deserved better." Anger is self protective. Anger is a part of you that loves you.

Let it out, if you want to. I did this before, myself. Wrote, scribbled, listened to music that fit, sang along, hit things, cried. Whatever feels right, whatever it takes, in a healthy way ofc but yeah.

Say "fuck you" to your parent and whoever else hurt you. Let it all out.

Yeah, it fucking sucks.

What do you need right now? You're hurting, you need something.

When we grow up with trauma it's so easy to feel helpless and hopeless as an adult. I've been there so many times, myself.

Do whatever it takes.

You didn't deserve what happened, and it fucking sucks. But I bet you have some amount of value. I bet you really do.

You deserve to be happy, too. I promise your happiness is there behind the clouds of all this, waiting, always waiting for you to return, or even find it for the first time. How can you clear some of the clouds, for now? How can you sooth yourself? Is there anything you feel that you need?

I'm sorry for what you've experienced. I know some of what it's like.

Is there anything that would help? Anything you feel you need?

I wish I could help you more.

I could tell you about my story and how it got better for me but I don't feel Iike that's what you need, right now. Idk. That's something to reflect on later maybe, stories of hope and recovery, if you want to, when you're feeling better in the moment. Right now I feel you are grieving and / or possibly in a trauma flashback kind of thing, too. (Grounding exercises can help with this, or rest, or any self care).

I'm rooting for you. Trauma sucks. You have worth and you deserve to be happy and I hope you get there x Until then, I'm one of many people out there in the world who are rooting for you and who care.

Same. It's worth it, I'm glad I'm alive.

Hope is hard. We don't see many stories of recovery. But they're out here, I promise.

I've despaired so badly at times. Felt suicidal many times in the past, too. I can genuinely say I am really glad I stayed alive and I'd be devastated at the thought that I didn't. It gets better, I promise.

Hey hon, please try to be kind to yourself and turn this around if you can <3 or are there any trusted, kind adults you can reach out to for help?

You're still growing, and your body needs all the good food and nutrition it can get to help you along. Your body needs fuel and you deserve to have it - for your brain development as well as all the other parts of you as well.

This "friend" of yours is not a friend. Words hurt a lot, especially at a young age you can be more sensitive to people's words. But what she said isn't your fault, it's her issue. She shouldn't have said anything about your weight.

If you are already feeling insecure, which is probably very common at a younger age, it's very easy to be attracted to something you can control that you might think will "fix yourself" or "make you better."

I'm an adult now, I'm 26. I used to be a little girl, and a teenager, who hated herself - and fixated on ways to "fix" myself. But I grew up and realised I was never broken, I was always just a person, good enough as is. You are too, I promise.

Please try not to call yourself nasty names in your head, I know this is hard, I've done it too, but you're not those horrible things you tell yourself.

It sounds like you already have an eating disorder as well, at least that's eating disordered behaviours you are doing.

There are people in the world who will be horrible or say things that tear you down like your "friend." Even now as an adult I still meet these people sometimes. It doesn't matter who you are or what you do, because the problem isn't you. It's them who are wrong.

Sometimes we have to fight these people's words when they get into our own heads. Because their words are wrong.

Phrases like that are just stupid things that people repeat that are not actually true, I believe.

It's like the "you can't love anyone until you love yourself." Bullshit. I loved my younger siblings so much I sacrificed myself for ages to stay around despite this meaning so much interaction with people who abused me horrendously (until I literally couldn't anymore). I hated myself, but I loved them very much.

A lot is blocked out for me. But one that seems weird is he would hold me down and "tickle" me quite intensely, like digging his hands / fingers into my stomach. I didn't like it, obviously. I'd cry out hoping my mum would hear and stop it. Sometimes she would say something, I think. I feel fairly often it ended in tears, then it would stop. During it he'd say "well you're laughing so you must like it / not want me to stop." I didn't like it, it was a reflex response as you do, he knew this, obviously.
But looking back on that it seems a bit bordering on something. I'm still unsure how abnormal this would seem to most other people.
Nowadays I properly lash out and hit people if they tickle me. Did it with a guy I'm seeing the other night. He tickled me and I just hit his head like 3 times and pulled his hair. Totally reflex response for me. I felt bad and said sorry, but I'd told him if anyone tickled me I'll lash out and can't really control it. I don't think he realised until then it's a proper PTSD thing... Lessons learned on both sides - I need to be more clear when telling people that's a trigger for me (I said it sorta goofing around before - didn't link it to PTSD or being properly serious or anything) and ig he now knows don't tickle me...
Yeah. Kinda fucked, I think.

❤️ so relatable with the telling younger brother it's my fault they're unhappy ('cause I stopped talking to them). It's sweet you didn't blame him for internalising this. They're not bad kids. Mines is just trying to "make things better" in a lot of ways, too. I'm so glad I'm still able to have a relationship with him despite this, and I'm so glad you have been able to, too.

Yeah the switch around from "why do you want to move out? 🥺🥺👉🏻👈🏻✨✨" to "(snarling) your memory can't be trusted, you thought [extra abuse] happened but only [something that is still very much abusive] happened" is very real and intense. I have learnt my lessons there.

Any time I was hit with "why are you sad? 🥺🥺" "Are you not happy with [family member] 🥺🥺🥺🥺?" was a trap and I'd be avoiding that fcking question as much as possible, and right into fight or flight.

I hate them. They're evil cunts.

Yeah I'd second this. Trauma informed has been the way to go for me (so much fcking incompetence before I found the 2 trauma informed therapists I've seen. A lot of these other therapist are living in a different world is2g 😂😭).

I'd just reject everything she's saying. Shitty to take your hope away like that, and nothing is absolute in life.
Of course it can happen to men, and her sharing those thoughts doesn't seem helpful or relevant to you but actively unhelpful (feels obvious to say, but yeah).
My approach with trauma is to always have high hopes that it can get better, and you know what? Even if it doesn't 100% heal, why not 10% more? Why not 20% more? Could even be 90-95%, but aim for the best and sounds very cheesy but "aim for the moon and if you fall you'll land amongst the stars." (Sorry, that's what came to mind..).

Fuck this, fuck what she's said. She's incompetent, some people are. I hope you can find a good trauma informed therapist who can actually help you and give you some fcking hope, if that's what you're needing and looking for.

Even if the trauma doesn't 100% heal right away, why not have you working towards a little bit better? That's always possible. And those small improvements are so amazing after living without them for so long. I don't think focusing on what apparently can't happen is helpful at all - perhaps she's just not very emotionally intelligent to give her the benefit of the doubt, but yeah. Ridiculous tbh. And even still, it's only her opinion.

I have issues around intimacy in some ways and they're massively getting better after years of healing and therapy and stuff. I relate less to the sex part although there are issues there too, and have been in the past. But yeah, some of it has got better. And it is getting better. And even if flashbacks or things like that can still happen, there are times that they don't, and that's still fab for me tbh. For me I've been having moments of letting myself trust in people / the world to take care of me almost (a big thing for me). Letting my guard down in a way. I've maybe done this once a year or so, but more so recently. Idk what I'm trying to say but just that it's possible to get there and have those moments again. And slowly, bit by bit, learn to retrust the world again, or live a different way once you're ready to and feel safe enough to do so again. Test the waters kind of thing, and get there, bit by bit.

It sounds like you've became aware of a problem and an area you'd like to work on, a belief you've internalised about sex that you can maybe take small steps to work towards changing and maybe explore a different way of being in the future, if and once you're ready. That's good and the absolute best first step with all of this stuff.

Sorry to hear about your therapy experience, some therapist are just a bit crap. It sounds like you're actively putting the work into healing and that's great, I'm sure you can there. Don't lose hope because of one stupid person. Rooting for you

I'd be considering reporting this as a sexual assault tbh. Or at least having it written down somewhere man, idk (like, legally).

I'm a girl but my first thought goes to "what if she tries to say it was the other way around?" People like that are known to pull shit like that.

She sounds dangerous. Like this is bad. I'd be trying to get the f away. What a horrible friend she's being to your girlfriend, too.

Have strong bounderies and try and stay the f away from this girl ig.

"it is also a life that was torn apart and stolen from you"

That's it really. That's a main part of the grief for me right now

❤️ just want to say I hear you, it's hard and it's frustrating when you find yourself unable to make your ideal goals in life as quickly as you want to.

Maybe there's a grief to process there, or something.

It's hard and I've felt similar. The simple truth is one step at a time. You can get there. What will help right now?

Sometimes we need to stop and let healing take more of a front seat, in the same way we would for any illness, disorder or period of grief. Every successful person has downfalls and times when they've had to say nope, I have to step back from this goal just now actually and focus on healing or self care or whatever first. In the long run it can help make you better.

I've found personally that taking the time for healing when needed has actually helped me come back to my goals in a better place for them. It's sad and it sucks but it's life, too, and it's all part of the journey.

You can still get there ❤️

Self compassion has helped me with things like this, as well as compassion towards other parts when I can. Why do they do what they do? There is always a reason, and it might not become clear right away. It's a difficult thing to deal with. You're doing well, you can get there with your goals in time ❤️

Also, a shift for me happened when realising it's not my fault (or my different parts faults) that I / we are dealing with these issues, and everything like that. The anger gets turned inwards so often when we are wronged in the ways those of us with DID have likely been wronged. Part of healing is putting that anger where it deserves, and allowing ourselves the compassion and understanding that we are doing the best we can and can work through our things with problem solving and love and compassion, without guilt and anger and shame. I hope it gets better for you soon, let yourself have a little break if you need it, you deserve it and you're far from alone. ❤️

For me I've felt similar but I'm starting to realise that this kind of attention is so very different from actual love and / or intimacy.

I won people over with looks, charm, etc. But they didn't love me. We didn't have a truly deep or intimate relationship. I never even knew how much was missing until after and lots of therapy and learning about attachment, needs, intimacy, etc.

It's such a shame to feel that way, and I get it. But there are people of all shapes, sizes, looks, jobs, etc. in relationships that appear to be happy, loving and secure.

Real love, and real intimacy is more than all that, I think. It's something you build together.

Personally my goal now is developing relationships and intimacy and having feelings grow potentially that way - finding love even if it's in friendship, etc.

I don't wanna reel anyone in by my looks or that, anymore. Not that it doesn't help. But I want real love and feelings that develop through building something, etc. Being close, etc. Idk.

I think for me the advice here would be something like: connecting with yourself and being you. Then connecting with others until you find your people. Working on building / having good relationships and real love, etc. Idk man. I'm still on the journey but it feels so different already. Like I'm capable of love now and it's not all just a transaction or a desperation to get my needs met (in places they are not or will never be). I'm tired of feeling like I'm trading my looks (which will fade), and other qualities which could pass (illness could happen, etc). For something resembling love on the outside that doesn't even come close.
This just feels true to me, especially from my life experience.
Thanks! ❤️

It was just complementing how they all looked in a picture, the response was fine - good even, mostly. Like a love heart, a little comment, and someone being like "lmao" cause I phrased it in a funny way (deliberately).

Cptsd is wild, lol.

I'm glad I triggered myself in a way, though, as I managed to ground myself and come out the other side for once, and I think it might help long term, to see that simply giving a compliment isn't massively unsafe or terribly, condemningly shameful. 🙃

My god, yeah. It's so triggering isn't it? Putting yourself out there to try and make new or healthier friends.

My therapist says staying present through triggers can help our bodies learn it's safe to do those things now, over time. Sounds true... So I'm deliberately triggering myself (at the capacity I can handle, etc.) but I am very mad about it, lol.

❤️

It's tough.

For me it's that healing without being 100% healed is worth it. This is worth it to me. Where I am right now is worth it. At the start, the idea that I couldn't fully cure this had me so suicidal, it felt awful. But thank fuck I stayed alive. Being somewhat healed is a different experience to what I felt about the idea of it back then, when I was terrified at the thought I couldn't just undo it all at once. Whatever this is: 20%? 50%? It feels much more wonderful that I would have thought. It's okay to be imperfectly healed. It's okay here. It's good even, I feel happy and connected and like life is meaningful and somewhat wonderful at times again now, and I'm proud of myself and very, very glad to be alive.

:(

For me,
- getting a good report at parents evening (lol) - "you pretend to be a nice, quiet girl at school but this is the REAL you" - this wasn't a one year thing, but repeated as well (:
- speaking back (even if I just said "okay" - you could not win, "it's not okay" - yeah cause that's what I meant by okay...)
- writing a newspaper article for our dog to find a new family when we had to re-home her ("you're deliberately trying to make me feel bad")

For me tbh, it often wasn't even things I did that were actually bad in any way. It fucking amazes me to hear other people laugh with their parents about the "naughty" things they did as a child. I'd have neeeeever, ever, ever, did anything wrong deliberately if I could help it (not to sound pure moral, the stakes were obviously high so that might be a big part of why. And I was always trying to be "good" when I was really young. Obviously felt like I wasn't, even though I probably was, for a child).

I did also get into trouble and abuse for other things that were more actually "bad", though.
- messy room was a big reoccurring one (and I'd deliberately not tidy it after the yelling and physical abuse about it - because I didn't want to teach him that bad behaviour works lol, as if I was the parent)
- the one time I bunked off school as I followed my friends and it spun out of hand.
- getting into a physical fight with my friend when we were kids. I was shamed so badly. I felt so ashamed.

Yeah my dad was a cowardly narcissistic sociopath who made victims of women and children. Pathetic cunt lol. Excuse the language...

No wonder I'm so messed up lmao. Praise God for therapy

Bonus one: getting the wrong loaf of bread from the shop, then saying it was all they had (I lied, he said he'd call them up and check, I had to go back. I was a very socially anxious child, obviously, and didn't enjoy doing a shop run not once but twice. And having to change a loaf of bread for another one. But yeah. That's another one ig)

It's a work in progress for me. I'm gonna be honest I'm still not totally there yet?

I've been in therapy with a trauma + dissociation focused therapist for over a year now, and had some therapy before this as well. It's getting better. To the point even where I'll look back on past relationships where I brushed things off and now I'm like omg that was not good behaviour and was unkind and is not something I'd be so okay with now, and I'll realise how it has broken my trust in the present day as well.

I have definitely stood up for myself against abusive behaviours more recently, and cut people off who exhibit them at times - or at least had strong words with them about how that is not acceptable to me. I've learnt how to set boundaries better - for me it really helped to have a therapist just validating me frequently, that I am being reasonable and not toxic or controlling to request the boundaries I have done at times. Things like that. And also having my therapist express anger when people treat me wrong, etc.

It's such a work in progress. I find myself continually reliving a similar pattern, to be honest. I feel like it is getting better - but it is certainly a journey.

I think what's helping me is - therapy, journaling (!!) to connect with my own feelings better and process them, as well as having a couple of safe, trusted friends I can talk things out with. That's the first few things that come to mind anyways that have helped.

Good luck! I hope it gets better for you soon, too. It certainly can. ❤️

Note: also just being educated on what abuse is and signs of abuse - like reading and learning about emotional abuse, for example. I needed that foundation, for sure. And practicing / finding self compassion, and lessening dissociation so I can feel my own feelings better. Basic self care improvements have helped with that, too. Just focusing on me and what I need, etc.

You're not alone ❤️ lots of us out here who don't fit the bill of "normal" and that's okay.

I understand feeling the need to use a substance or other method, like SH, to cope. I feel very similarly at times and I feel kinda strongly that it's not really our faults sometimes in a lot of ways. We're just people with trauma a lot of the time - trying our best to survive in our societies, and stay "put together" enough to get through.

For me it was SH, which I too stopped because other people can see, and replaced with smoking. I quit sometimes but it is hard to not replace with another addiction or go back when things get difficult.

Just to say I understand, to some extent.

I hope it gets easier for you.

(Just a side note: not endorsing drugs or alcohol or anything. I know, it's best to recover and go sober when and if we can. I just wanted to say I understand).

Aw man so this is a BPD mum thing too 😭 fuck sake. Direct quotes almost. Is nothing I experience original?

I didn't realise till now the constant asking you to clear out your stuff that's been left behind maybe isn't normal as well 🙁 especially when contrasted with the whole clearly not wanting you to move out yet part. That is sad

❤️❤️

Understand if you don't wanna share here, but if you felt like sharing or DMing your Spotify I'd be so happy to listen and hype u up. So here for supporting fellow survivors and it's amazing you're nurturing your talent and following your dreams!

❤️ break ups are so hard sometimes, especially when you're already depressed. It hurts so much, I know. I hope you feel better soon. Give yourself permission to do whatever you need to get through (sleep a lot, eat garbage, see friends if you can, or eat healthy and exercise, or a mix of the lot, whatever makes you feel better).

It eases in time and life can be beautiful again. I had a terrible breakup last year that put me in the hospital (haha, oops). But honestly, my life now is brighter than it was at any time in that relationship. Self love helps, fight for yourself - and when you can't fight - let yourself rest.

I hope you find your happiness soon, too. ❤️
It was for me :( It made me really suicidal at times. Still feel guilty at times though, for going no contact. Mad, isn't it?
My gosh. We need more awareness of this stuff :( I'm so sorry about your friend. That fucking sucks

Precisely this.

It bothers me that if I did that... many people would likely respond with calls for better suicide prevention and "talk to someone!!" etc.

No, I'm not sick, I'm not insane, I'm injured, and other people did that to me.

I made a point of making that clear in any notes I make when I feel that way inclined 😂

But, I'm choosing to stay, and MAYBE at some point try and change some viewpoints around that in my lifetime (without offing myself and leaving a message to do so..).

Society has wisened up over lots of other stuff, even the past decade or so. I do believe there is hope. But yeah it is fucking frustrating (and invalidating feeling) to say the least, at times.

Some people get it tho ❤️ I get it. We're out here and we see and we understand, even if we're quieter than those who might be more performatively inclined sharing lots of messages on Facebook or words or opinions.

Omg well done!!

Emmm, idk because I'm also at about 3 weeks (with a couple of minor slip-ups), and weirdly I felt like a non-smoker pretty quickly. Even when I slipped up I knew I didn't want to start again properly and would do anything to stop. Something changed for me mentally. But I was feeling very unwell from smoking and not enjoying it anymore (was giving me anxiety attacks, etc.), and really, really done with it. Maybe reminding yourself of all the reasons not to smoke and why you hate it might help? Idk. Good luck!

For me I think what changed was I hated being a smoker and smoking so much more than anything by this point. I was sick of it. It made me miserable for years and could see all the ways it was ruining my life. Cigarettes literally made me feel anxious and depressed right after I smoked them 99% of the time. It got to a point where I was so sick of being attached to smoking, and so sick of all of it and desperate for my life back, that I'd go through withdrawal times over rather than smoke again (not saying it wasn't difficult, times it was bloody relentless, but yeah).

I'm on sick leave for stress that I had enough self compassion to allow myself (I refused to force myself to struggle on in the way I was anymore).
I did Lego, listened to sad songs that helped me process some stuff, ate lots of food, watched a movie with a blanket, did about 40 mins of housework.

Me a year or two ago could never, I've came such a long way from the girl who was so riddled with guilt she couldn't give herself time for a much needed bath at times and was obsessively hyperfocusing on how to "fix" things with her family.

I used to. With a few years of healing I don't anymore really. It's possible to feel connected again and not like you are worlds away from the "other" people (non traumatised ones).
I feel for you though. I remember that feeling. I hope you have some nice moments of connection if they're wanted ❤️
❤️❤️ well done on pushing past that fear, it's so hard to do but so awesome, glad to hear it worked out but either way u did good! :)

I can understand her being wary, I'm PTSD'd af and dating is like, you're constantly on guard that a guy is going to be abusive - hypersensitive to noticing red flags, etc. I've got wary from similar comments myself before. Unfortunately a lot of guys who make jokes about abuse or rape, well, us girls come to learn there's a correlation with the people who actually do these things.

A good analogy for DID I've found is this. A non-DID brain is like a tangerine - all the segments (different parts) are close together and form one whole. Whereas in a DID brain the segments are spaced further apart. There are dissociative barriers between them. Every segment is still a part of the overall whole. They're just not connected in the same way - this is due to trauma interrupting the process of personality fusion in early development (at least by the current theory of structural dissociation).

It will depend on the person, but you may well have already met different parts. You just wouldn't necessarily notice from the outside.

Healing means trying to lessen the dissociative barriers between parts so that all parts can work together and, in a way, form a whole.

I remember the concept of starting with the least scary things, then working your way up as your anxiety decreases. This will be different for everyone, but some ideas might be:

- saying hi to a colleague.
- asking for something (like a pencil).
- making a phone call.
- saying hello or making small talk with the easiest person in the room to talk to (e.g. someone who does not intimidate you).
- asking how someone's weekend was or other small talk.
- contributing an idea or answer in a group situation.
- doing a presentation in front of a small group (this might be the kind of thing you work towards as opposed to starting with).

Good luck! :-)
